interest: This file provides valuable historical insight into the growing commercial and diplomatic friction between the United States and Japan during the 1930s, centering on intellectual property rights, counterfeiting, and unfair trade practices. It illustrates how Japanese manufacturers aggressively imitated American products and exploited legal ambiguities, including notorious controversies over marking goods 'Made in USA' (claimed to refer to the Japanese town of Usa in Oita Prefecture or 'United States of Asia') and Japanese matchboxes marked 'Made in Sweden'. Furthermore, the purport lists document the internal legal reasoning of the State Department, Department of Commerce, Tariff Commission, and Federal Trade Commission, illuminating the strict limits of U.S. diplomatic intervention when American firms failed to register trademarks domestically in Japan or when infringing goods were sold exclusively in third-country markets such as Egypt, India, China, and Hong Kong.
overview: This file consists of U.S. State Department 'List of Papers' (docket and purport index sheets) filed under decimal number 894.543 and its related jacket cases, spanning 1932 to 1939 with a 1945 docket cover. The records index correspondence, despatches, legal opinions, and complaints handled by the Department of State, the Department of Commerce, the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo, and various consular offices concerning Japanese trademark infringements, patent conflicts, and deceptive commercial practices. Major American companies represented in these files include General Electric, Celluloid Corporation, Samuel M. Dell & Company, The Embossing Company, Fostoria Pressed Steel, Greenfield Tap & Die, Holeproof Hosiery, Mallinckrodt Chemical Works, Monarch Engineering & Manufacturing, Standard Oil Development Company (Paraflow), and The Parker Pen Company. A prominent recurring issue involves Japanese manufacturers marking goods 'Made in USA' or using American insignia, disingenuously asserting that 'USA' represented either the Japanese town of Usa or the 'United States of Asia', alongside Japanese statutory developments including the Law for the Prevention of Unfair Competition and amendments to the Japanese Trade Mark Law.

subfiles.about: Purport list indexing general correspondence and despatches concerning Japanese trademark issues, unfair competition, and misleading 'Made in USA' labeling between 1933 and 1939.
subfiles.summary: These index sheets cover general sub-numbers 20 through 45 under decimal file 894.543. Major matters catalogued include fraudulent stamping of Japanese light bulbs, deceptive needle booklets featuring American national insignia and the battleship Iowa, and extensive inquiries from American businesses, citizens, and government agencies regarding Japanese products deceptively marked 'Made in USA' attributed to the Japanese town of Usa. The list also records reports from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew on Japan's 1934 and 1938 trademark law revisions and the Law for the Prevention of Unfair Competition.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Trademarks - Japan (General File 894.543, Sub-numbers 20-45)

subfiles.about: Docket entry concerning allegations of Japanese exports to China of lead pencils imitating an American trademark.
subfiles.summary: This single-entry purport list records a communication from the National Recovery Administration regarding Japanese exports to China of pencils marked to imitate an American trademark. The paper was cross-referenced to decimal file 611.003-Lead Pencils/26.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Trade-marks, trade-names of the American Pencil Institute in Japan

subfiles.about: Purport list documenting complaints and legal discussions regarding Japanese infringement of the Celluloid Corporation's trademark 'CELLULOID'.
subfiles.summary: This jacket case list details efforts by attorney Matthew H. O'Brien on behalf of the Celluloid Corporation of Newark, New Jersey, to halt Japanese firms from circulating sales catalogues and solicitations in the United States using the mark 'Welluloid' or 'Celluloid'. The State Department advised that because the mark was not registered in Japan and no U.S. judicial finding of infringement had been obtained, there was no tenable basis for diplomatic representations. The Post Office Department also evaluated the matter under existing postal treaties and fraud order statutes, finding insufficient evidence to issue a fraud order.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Infringement of trade-mark 'CELLULOID' of the Celluloid Corp. of Newark, N.J., by Japanese

subfiles.about: Purport list recording inquiries by the American Brush Manufacturers Association regarding Japanese infringement of Samuel M. Dell & Company's trademark 'DELL'.
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet records correspondence from George A. Fernley of the American Brush Manufacturers Association reporting Japanese infringement of the trademark 'DELL' belonging to Samuel M. Dell & Company. The Department of State, concurring with advice from the Department of Commerce, recommended that the company consult trademark attorneys with correspondents in Tokyo. Repeated communications ensured transmission of the Department's guidance.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Infringement of Trade-Mark of the Samuel M. Dell Company, in Japan

subfiles.about: Purport list detailing the illicit export from Japan to Egypt of automobile electric light bulbs fraudulently bearing the 'Edison' brand.
subfiles.summary: This jacket sheet indexes despatches between the American Consulate in Alexandria, Egypt, the Embassy in Tokyo, and the State Department regarding Alexandria merchant Jacques I. Sciarbit importing Japanese automobile bulbs bearing the brand 'Edison' from a Japanese manufacturer. The State Department determined that International General Electric Company of Tokyo held the exclusive right to the name 'Edison' in Japan and advised that legal action should be initiated by that company. Consular reports from Tokyo confirmed the communication of these findings to the consulate in Alexandria.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Exportation from Japan of electric bulbs fraudulently stamped 'Edison'

subfiles.about: Purport list concerning the copying of The Embossing Company's embossed toys and slogan 'Toys that Teach' by Japanese competitors.
subfiles.summary: This jacket case covers complaints by Lewis S. Greenleaf, President of The Embossing Company of Albany, New York, regarding Japanese copying of embossed toys and novelties and unauthorized use of the slogan 'Toys that Teach'. State Department economic and legal advisers consulted with the U.S. Tariff Commission and the Federal Trade Commission regarding possible remedies under Section 337 of the Tariff Act or international conventions. The Department concluded, with White House concurrence, that no administrative or legal remedy was available until unfairly competing goods actually entered the customs territory of the United States.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Infringement of Trade Mark or Trade Name of The Embossing Company, in Japan

subfiles.about: Purport list detailing Japanese manufacture and export to India of automobile replacement fenders bearing Fostoria Pressed Steel trademarks.
subfiles.summary: This jacket case indexes correspondence from The Fostoria Pressed Steel Corporation regarding a Japanese competitor manufacturing replacement automobile fenders and shipping them into India under Fostoria's trademark and parts numbers. The company also sought protection for introducing its product 'Fostoria TiteSeal' into the Asian market. The State Department responded that informal discussions through the Tokyo Embassy required specific evidence and noted that absent registration in Japan or India, remedial action was doubtful.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Infringement of the Trade Mark of the Fostoria Pressed Steel Corporation in Japan

subfiles.about: Purport entry regarding Japanese public opposition and protests against General Electric Company's electric light bulb patents.
subfiles.summary: This docket entry indexes a despatch from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo transmitting a translated leaflet issued by the 'Society Opposing the General Electric Patents'. The leaflets were distributed at a mass protest meeting in Tokyo against patent applications filed by the General Electric Company governing the manufacture of electric light bulbs. The papers were cross-referenced to general decimal files 894.543 and 894.4016.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Trade-marks - Patents, General Electric Co. in Japan

subfiles.about: Purport list recording the diplomatic and legal dispute surrounding the Japanese Patent Bureau's rejection of Greenfield Tap & Die Corporation's 'GTD' trademark.
subfiles.summary: Covering two pages, this jacket list documents Greenfield Tap & Die Corporation's protest after the Japanese Patent Bureau refused registration of its trademark 'GTD in panel with name' due to a prior registration granted to a Japanese subject in apparent disregard of Greenfield's earlier Japanese registrations. Working through Chairman Frederick H. Payne and patent attorneys Edwards, Bower & Pool, the company submitted arguments and photostats to the State Department. The Department instructed Ambassador Grew and the Tokyo Embassy to make representations to appropriate Japanese authorities to seek a reversal of the Patent Bureau's decision.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Infringement of Trademark GTD, of Greenfield Tap and Die Corporation Japan

subfiles.about: Purport list concerning the fraudulent use of 'Made in U.S.A.' by Japanese exporters, falsely explained as standing for 'United States of Asia'.
subfiles.summary: This jacket list details complaints by the Holeproof Hosiery Company and its commercial agent, Ed. A. Keller & Co., Ltd., regarding Japanese exporters labeling goods 'Made in U.S.A.' and defending the mark as signifying 'United States of Asia'. The State Department instructed the American Consul in Hong Kong, Louis E. Gourley, to investigate and identify the offending Japanese firms with a view toward seeking suppression of the practice by Japanese authorities. Related despatches from Bangkok noted similar deceptive merchandise masquerading as American products in Southeast Asia.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Infringement of Trade Mark of the Holeproof Hosiery Company, of New York City, by Japanese exporters in Japan

subfiles.about: Purport entry regarding the unauthorized registration of the Mallinckrodt script trademark in Japan and related narcotic concerns.
subfiles.summary: This single entry records a Treasury Department communication transmitting a letter from Mallinckrodt Chemical Works regarding the registration of its script trademark in Japan by Siber, Hegner & Company of Yokohama. The communication highlighted the potential complications and regulatory risks concerning narcotics, cross-referencing the matter to narcotic file 811.114 N 16 - Mallinckrodt Chemical Works/323.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Trade Marks - Trade Names, of the Mallinckrodt Chemical Works in Japan

subfiles.about: Purport list documenting Monarch Engineering & Manufacturing Company's request for State Department assistance against trademark piracy in Japan.
subfiles.summary: This jacket list indexes an urgent request by The Monarch Engineering & Manufacturing Company of Baltimore for State Department assistance regarding a Japanese competitor filing an application in Japan to register the trademark 'MONARCH'. The company warned that the statutory period for filing an opposition expired on January 6, 1936. The State Department requested additional supporting evidence to establish legal infringement under Japanese law and emphasized the urgent necessity of expeditious filing.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Infringement of trade-mark 'MONARCH' of The Monarch Engineering & Manufacturing Co., Baltimore, Maryland

subfiles.about: Purport list recording the diplomatic efforts and legal appeals of Standard Oil Development Company to register its 'PARAFLOW' trademark in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Spanning two pages, this jacket list details extensive efforts by Standard Oil Development Company attorney H. M. McLarin to overcome the Japanese Patent Office's rejection of the 'PARAFLOW' design and word mark in favor of a competing registration by a Japanese applicant named Nagai. The State Department instructed the Embassy at Tokyo to make representations to the Japanese Foreign Office, supporting legal briefs and arguments filed by Japanese attorneys in Osaka. In July 1938, after the Japanese Appeal Board upheld the rejection, the State Department concluded that there was no longer an adequate legal basis for further diplomatic intervention.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Registration of PARAFLOW DESIGN in Japan

subfiles.about: Purport list detailing The Parker Pen Company's persistent complaints against Japanese counterfeiting of its fountain pens, trademarks, and patents.
subfiles.summary: Spanning two pages, this jacket case chronicles extensive friction between The Parker Pen Company, the State Department, and the Tokyo Consulate General regarding Japanese counterfeiting of Parker pens and imitation of its subsidiary trade name, the Safford Pen Company. Parker officials George S. Parker and Ivan D. Tefft protested the rejection of Parker's laminated pen patent by the Japanese Patent Office and sharply criticized U.S. diplomatic officials for perceived inaction. Consular investigations in Tokyo initially uncovered insufficient physical evidence to lodge formal protests, but continued coordination between the State Department and the Department of Commerce sought viable legal grounds to bring Parker's grievances before the Japanese government.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Infringement of trade name of The Parker Pen Co.
